placements.why: Existing strata is empty for this repo. This envelope's content is fundamentally a governance act — a named individual (Quinton Fairweather) declaring, scoping, and owning a mandatory control over Meridian's deployment process. That is organizational-accountability content, not a fact about a single deploy; it names the kind of category ('who owns and governs what process') that future envelopes about roles, ownership, and process control will keep feeding. Nothing in the (empty) existing strata or graph structure could hold this, so a NEW strata mint is required rather than a leaf directly under nothing.
placements.title: Release-control ownership becomes an organizational accountability domain
placements.frame: Which organizational roles and processes hold accountability for release, deployment, and operational governance?

placements.title: Meridian deploys shift from unsigned shipping to mandatory signed-manifest gating
placements.frame: What is the current mandate, scope, and accountable owner of the Meridian deployment gate, and how does that specification change as it is revised or extended?
placements.why: src-1's opening declaration that Meridian 'now requires a signed release manifest before it ships,' and the labeled Gate/Scope/Owner triad in src-3–src-5, together specify a standing policy — what's required, where it applies, and who is accountable for it. This is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (amendments to the gate, scope changes, owner handoffs), not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test. Nothing existing (graph structure is empty) covers deployment-gate policy, so this is a NEW mint, placed under the freshly-minted Organization strata since it is fundamentally an accountability/process-control specification.

placements.title: Past release failures become the cited justification for imposing new deployment controls
placements.frame: What specific incidents or failures are being invoked to justify a control, and how does that cited rationale hold up or get revisited as the control persists?
placements.why: src-2 ('We saw two unsigned artifacts reach staging last quarter and that is the whole reason for the gate') is a concrete past incident offered as causal justification for the policy in Narrative_MeridianDeploymentGatePolicy — its conviction sits at 'claim' rather than 'decision', its register is plain-spoken rather than protocol-formal, and it is concrete-past rather than abstract-present, so it is defending the mandate rather than constituting it (consistent with the position pass excluding it from GateMandateDeclaration). Per the grain rule, a one-time incident is evidence, not its own leaf — but the recurring pattern it instantiates ('cited incidents justify new controls') is a subject that generalizes beyond this specific pair of artifacts and that future envelopes are likely to keep feeding with other incident-justified controls, so it clears the grain test as its own thematic container distinct from the policy specification itself.
